candidates.title: TSS trust-root rotation has no timelock/two-step; single privileged key can redirect custody/mint authority
candidates.description: updateTSSAddress (custody, onlyTSSUpdater), updateTssAddress (connector: current tss can rotate itself), updateTssAndConnectorAddresses (ZetaNonEth: tss or updater) all atomically reassign the trust root with no delay; ZetaNonEth has no supply cap so the new connector can mint unbounded.

candidates.title: ERC20Custody.withdraw transfers exact amount, ignoring fee-on-transfer tokens (custody insolvency)
candidates.description: withdraw() does IERC20(asset).safeTransfer(recipient, amount) with the deposit-credited amount; deposit() uses a balance-delta but withdraw() does not, so for a fee-on-transfer whitelisted asset the contract pays out more than it net-received.

candidates.title: onReceive lacks whenNotPaused (pause does not halt inbound delivery); onRevert has it
candidates.description: onReceive is onlyTssAddress but NOT whenNotPaused, while onRevert IS whenNotPaused. Emergency pause cannot stop inbound token delivery/callbacks.

candidates.title: No internalSendHash replay/dedup tracking in connectors (double-delivery if TSS replays)
candidates.description: No mapping(bytes32=>bool) of processed internalSendHash; the same hash can be processed repeatedly. internalSendHash is only used in events / passed to mint() for tracing.

candidates.title: Uninitialized interactorsByChainId[chain] (empty bytes) lets empty zetaTxSenderAddress pass sender check
candidates.description: modifier compares keccak256(sender) vs keccak256(interactorsByChainId[srcChain]) without first asserting the interactor entry is set; both empty -> keccak256('')==keccak256('') passes. _isValidChainId(ZERO_BYTES) guard exists but is NOT used in the modifier.

candidates.title: Mint authority tied to mutable SYSTEM_CONTRACT_ADDRESS updated with no zero-address guard
candidates.description: deposit() mints, allowed for FUNGIBLE_MODULE or mutable SYSTEM_CONTRACT_ADDRESS; updateSystemContractAddress(onlyFungible) has NO zero/address validation, so the mint-authorised address can be set to any contract.

candidates.title: getEthFromZeta lacks nonReentrant while sending ETH to caller-controlled destinationAddress (cross-fn reentrancy)
candidates.description: getEthFromZeta swaps ZETA->WETH->ETH then destinationAddress.call{value}('') with NO nonReentrant (getTokenFromZeta has it). Re-entry into unguarded getZetaFromEth/getZetaFromToken is possible during the ETH callback. Same pattern in PancakeV3.

candidates.title: Trident strategy uses poolFactory.getPools(...)[0] with no length/zero/legitimacy validation
candidates.description: pairPools[0] used directly as the swap pool with no check that the array is non-empty or the pool is canonical; a front-run/permissionless factory entry could route swaps through an attacker pool, and an empty array reverts (DoS).

candidates.title: ERC20Custody.deposit zetaFee transfer not balance-checked (fee accounting drift for FoT zeta)
candidates.description: zeta.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, TSSAddress, zetaFee) without balance-delta; if zeta is fee-on-transfer, TSS receives < zetaFee while depositor is debited full fee.

candidates.title: withdrawGasFee has no GAS_LIMIT==0 / gasFee==0 guard (zero gas fee withdrawal)
candidates.description: gasFee = gasPrice*GAS_LIMIT + PROTOCOL_FLAT_FEE; guards check gasPrice!=0 and gasZRC20!=0 but not GAS_LIMIT==0; with GAS_LIMIT=0 and flat fee 0, transferFrom(...,0) succeeds and burn proceeds fee-free.

candidates.title: ZetaConnectorZEVM constructor has no FUNGIBLE_MODULE guard (anyone can deploy a connector instance)
candidates.description: Unlike ZRC20/SystemContract constructors which revert if msg.sender!=FUNGIBLE_MODULE, ZetaConnectorZEVM constructor is unguarded; a rogue instance can emit ZetaSent events of identical shape.

candidates.title: Swap deadline computed as block.timestamp+MAX_DEADLINE(200s); Trident path has no deadline (weak MEV protection)
candidates.description: deadline = block.timestamp + 200 is always satisfied at inclusion time, so it provides no staleness protection; Trident router params omit a deadline entirely. minAmountOut is the only slippage guard and depends on the caller.
